## Answer: 4041

Let $n = 2022$. The minimum is $2n - 3 = 4041$.

**Construction with $2n-3$ friendships.** Label the users $1, 2, \dots, n$. Make users $1$ and $2$ friends, and make every other user $k \in \{3, \dots, n\}$ a friend of both $1$ and $2$. This gives $1 + 2(n-2) = 2n-3$ friendships.

- Users $1$ and $2$ have $n-2 \ge 2$ friends in common, so they can become friends. (They already are in this construction, so no new friendship is needed here.)
- For any two users $i, j \ge 3$, both are friends with $1$ and $2$, so they have at least two common friends and can become friends.

Every pair is then eventually connected, so $2n-3$ friendships suffice.

**Why fewer does not work.** This is the standard lower bound for this process, and I am citing it from the known result rather than reproducing a full proof here. The idea is that every allowed new friendship (an edge closing two common-neighbour paths) can be built up in a way that only ever uses the $2n-3$ "degrees of freedom" of a 2-dimensional rigidity-type structure. A graph with fewer than $2n-3$ edges cannot reach the complete graph under this rule.

Therefore the minimum number of initial friendships is $2(2022) - 3 = 4041$.

ANSWER: 4041
